report:
PASS for conditional scope coverage only. If a separate, independent full correctness PASS establishes the exact round-48 theorem, its two retained-field versions cover P16.6 under section 10.2. This audit does not establish mathematical correctness or count P16.6 as actually solved.

The decisive original quotations are:

P16.6: “Prove the operator and existence-and-uniqueness theorem for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy measure
support beyond the known toric skeletal regime. Measures must satisfy the correct mass and
energy conditions. Do not reduce arbitrary support to a single skeleton or replace the genuine
Monge–Ampère measure by another inverse measure construction.”

Section 10.2: “For each axis, state the retained hypotheses and construct the ﬁnite-energy operator together
with the corresponding existence-and-uniqueness theorem. Specify the measure mass and
ﬁnite-energy condition, uniqueness modulo constants and the replacement inputs for com-
pactness, envelopes, energy diﬀerentiation and comparison. An endpoint solving a special
toric measure class does not remove a general axis.”

P16.4: “Extend the operator and existence theorem to nondiscrete valuations and arbitrary complete
non-Archimedean ﬁelds outside the established invariant-toric, skeleton-supported endpoint.
A deﬁnition of the ﬁnite-energy space alone does not establish the operator or the equation.”

Section 10.3: “This is not one yes-or-no assertion.” Its toric proposition starts: “Let K be a complete
nontrivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld, XΣ a proper toric K-variety, and L an ample toric
line bundle.” It then requires skeletal support, zero boundary mass, and the specified total mass. The explanatory paragraph states: “This is not an arbitrary-
ﬁeld ﬁnite-energy theorem in the BFJ sense: the result permits a singular potential, requires
torus invariance and skeletal support, and does not construct the general extended Monge–
Ampère operator. In particular, P16.4 and P16.6 retain the respectively nonskeletal and
noninvariant ﬁnite-energy residual scopes.”

These statements must be read together. P16.6 universally quantifies over admissible target measures within explicitly retained hypotheses. It prohibits narrowing their support to a skeleton or replacing genuine MA. P16.4 expressly adds the arbitrary-complete-field obligation. P16.6 contains no corresponding field quantifier, and section 10.2 expressly allows retained hypotheses for each axis. The arbitrary-field quantifier in Proposition 10.1 belongs to that proposition; its existence does not attach that quantifier to every other atom. The residual sentence preserves the noninvariant finite-energy obligation for P16.6, which an all-target theorem satisfies. It neither restricts P16.6 to invariant measures nor expressly requires combining P16.6 with P16.4.

Let C mean a separate full correctness PASS establishing both exact endpoint theorems, every necessary supporting proof, the correctness of the energy condition, and every essential external theorem application. C is an explicit antecedent, not an established premise here.

Under C, the theorem has the following quantifiers. Separately in T and D, for every field, variety and ample line bundle satisfying the stated retained hypotheses, and every dimension n≥1, every positive Radon measure µ of mass V=(L^n) with sup over model tests a of {VEθ(a)−∫a dµ}<∞ is Mθ(u) for some u∈E1. Every other E1 solution differs by a constant. The operator has exactly this range. The support quantifier is over all measures meeting the mass and energy conditions; it does not promise solutions for measures of infinite energy.

T retains an algebraically closed, trivially valued characteristic-zero field and a smooth connected integral projective variety. D retains a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero and a smooth geometrically integral projective variety. Thus the result does not silently assert coverage of non-algebraically-closed trivial fields, positive residue characteristic, or nondiscrete fields. These are expressly retained field hypotheses, rather than hidden exceptions to the measure quantifier.

| Required assumption or quantifier | Exact round-48 coverage, conditional on C | Missing P16.6 obligation |
|---|---|---|
| State retained geometric and field hypotheses | Section 1 specifies T and D, smoothness, integrality, projectivity, ampleness and references | None within those retained domains |
| Arbitrary dimension, without a curve restriction | Both endpoints cover every n≥1 | None in the stated positive-dimensional range |
| Every admissible measure, without a target-support restriction | Sections 5–6 cover every D target; section 7 states the corresponding T coverage | None |
| Beyond invariant toric and skeletal targets | Neither theorem assumes a torus action, invariance, skeletal support or retraction factorization | None |
| Correct mass and finite-energy condition | Sections 1, 5–6 and 7 specify raw mass V and finite dual energy, including its E1-integrability interpretation | None, provided C validates that condition |
| Genuine finite-energy MA operator | Section 3 constructs D through truncation and locality; section 7 describes T through the intersection pairing; both claim approximation independence and full mass | None under C |
| Existence and uniqueness modulo constants | Sections 6 and 7 claim realization of every admissible target and injectivity modulo constants | None under C |
| Compactness, envelopes, energy differentiation and comparison | D identifies the inputs in sections 2–4, proves the target-integration passage in section 5 and attainment in section 6; T identifies the corresponding inputs in section 7 | None under C; their validity remains a correctness question |
| Arbitrary complete fields and nondiscrete valuations | Not covered by T or D | An unresolved P16.4 obligation, not an additional literal P16.6 requirement |
| Singular, nonprojective, positive-residue-characteristic, nonample and nonalgebraizable settings | Not claimed | Separate P16.1, P16.2, P16.3, P16.5 and P16.7 obligations |

The complete family therefore permits retaining the hypotheses belonging to the other axes while removing the support restriction. The all-target quantifier matters: a special toric measure class would fail section 10.2, whereas the stated T/D theorem is unrestricted in support throughout its retained domains. Section 10.3's general-field endpoint remains insufficient for the unrestricted field theory, but that insufficiency does not supply a missing field quantifier in P16.6.

The author’s “partial” labels, the notes’ repeated scope judgments, and the root’s closure status were not used as evidence. Their assertion that P16.6 necessarily remains incomplete because arbitrary complete fields are untreated imports P16.4 into P16.6. The appropriate scope description is: “P16.6 is fully covered under explicitly retained T/D hypotheses, conditional on independent correctness; the arbitrary-field axis and unrestricted family remain unresolved.” This corrects scope wording without changing or repairing the mathematical theorem. Extending it to arbitrary complete fields would require a new mathematical argument.

No independent correctness PASS is established here. In particular, the draft’s source applications, orthogonality passage, test-to-E1 estimates, attainment, operator construction and uniqueness must all survive that separate audit. Conditional scope PASS therefore authorizes no present claim that the original atom is solved.

This scope implication is self-contained from the supplied original wording and candidate theorem. No external mathematical result is asserted as an established premise.
